Emily Chen: Quick question — updating the routing runbook for tier-based fallbacks. want to confirm intended behavior before I push docs.
Priya Nair: go for it, what's the gap?
Emily Chen: We currently fallback to the cheapest compatible variant when a preferred model is overloaded. But for Free tier we were going to *soft-deny* (quota error + suggest upgrade) instead of automatic fallback to lower-quality variant. Is that still the plan?
Jamal Ortiz: I thought we agreed soft-deny for free, auto-fallback for Pro, and guaranteed reserved variant for Enterprise.
Alex Green: That was the proposal in the last sync, yes. But we need an escape hatch: if Pro fallback latency >> primary, maybe route to enterprise-variant-with-throttling? odd edge case.
Priya Nair: we should be explicit in the policy schema. Example we can show in runbook:
```json
{
  "policy_name": "tiered_variant_fallback",
  "rules": [
    {"tier": "free", "on_quota_exhaust": "soft_deny", "fallback": null},
    {"tier": "pro", "on_quota_exhaust": "fallback", "fallback_order": ["variant-small","variant-medium"]},
    {"tier": "enterprise", "on_quota_exhaust": "route_to_reserved", "fallback_order": []}
  ]
}
```
Emily Chen: perfect. another open item: telemetry counters. ops wants metrics that map directly to console widgets so SRE can set alerts. what do we surface?
Ryan K.: minimal set: route_evaluations_total, fallback_hits_total, quota_denials_total, avg_fallback_latency_ms, percent_fallback_by_tier{tier}.
Jamal Ortiz: add tokens_consumed_by_variant and route_resolution_errors. also capture reason tags: RATE_LIMIT, CONNECTIVITY, KERNEL_OOM.
Alex Green: console UX: show a per-tenant small card: current plan, requests/min, fallback %, last 24h quota denials, and a link to runbook. Should be drillable to per-route and per-variant.
Emily Chen: good. Priya can we have alert thresholds in console config? e.g. fallback% > 5% for 10m => p95 latency increase alert?
Priya Nair: yes, we can wire a UI to create those alerts. Need the backend feature flag for per-tenant alerting (default off for free).
infra-bot: deploy-check: routing-config-service v2.8.1 passed canary in us-west-2 (build 2026-03-18T11:45Z) :white_check_mark:
Emily Chen: thanks infra-bot. last question: API surface for internal teams to preview routing decisions (so product can show "what would happen if I bump plan"). we had a draft endpoint earlier.
Priya Nair: draft is /internal/routing/preview POST {tenant_id, plan_override, region, model_request} => returns decision trace and cost/latency estimate.
Emily Chen: can we add a small example trace for the runbook?
Jamal Ortiz: example:
```
{
  "decision": "fallback_to_variant-medium",
  "trace": ["resolved pool: pro-us-west","variant choice: variant-medium","quota_check: pass","fallback_reason: capacity_threshold"],
  "est_cost_tokens": 120,
  "est_tail_latency_ms": 320
}
```
Alex Green: one more ops-safety thought: when we rollout any policy change we should have auto-rollback if fallback_hits spike > 25% within 5m for top-10 tenants. simple canary guard.
Priya Nair: agreed. we'll bake that into the rollout job and expose a toggle in the console rollout modal.
Emily Chen: action items: 1) Priya: add schema example + alert hooks to runbook. 2) Jamal: add telemetry metrics to metrics PR. 3) Alex: design console card mockups. 4) Ryan: add canary guard to rollout job. I'll update the doc and ping when it's live.
Ryan K.: noting: add histogram for fallback_latency_ms too.
Priya Nair: will do.
Emily Chen: thanks all. if no objections I’ll push to /docs/runbooks/routing-policy.md and link from console. :thumbsup:
Alex Green: +1
Jamal Ortiz: +1
Ryan K.: +1
infra-bot: deploy-queue: config docs changes queued for docs-site (next deploy window)
